summary: @ornikar/eslint-plugin-neverthrow ships a preinstall Bun-runtime dropper that executes an obfuscated bundled payload
details: The package presents itself as an ESLint plugin but its `preinstall` script `setup.mjs` downloads the Bun runtime from GitHub releases, extracts it to a temp directory, marks it executable, and uses it to run a sibling file `math_init.js`. `math_init.js` is a 727 KB `// @bun @bun-cjs` bundle whose strings are reconstructed at runtime through a shuffled character table and permutation function (`WV8StW`), so its behavior cannot be inspected without execution. The bundle is not referenced from the plugin's own `dist/src/index.js`; its sole invocation is from the preinstall dropper. An ESLint plugin has no legitimate need to fetch a second language runtime at install time to execute an opaque, obfuscated blob, and the alternate-runtime step bypasses scanners that only inspect Node-resolved code. Installing this version runs attacker-supplied code on the installer's host under the user account performing `npm install`.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
